sentences.text: Yamanasaurus possessed a stocky, quadrupedal body featuring an elongated neck and tail, reaching an estimated length of 6 meters or 20 feet.
Like other saltasaurines, this animal likely sported protective armor composed of osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin.
This species holds the distinction of being the first non-avian dinosaur formally described from Ecuador.
The discovery began when an octogenarian resident named Francisco Celi found a single vertebra in 2017.
Professor Galo Guamán and his students officially identified the holotype—the specimen the species is based on—in that same year.
Guamán later established the fossil's age by correlating the rock samples with those from the Maastrichtian period.
Evidence suggests Yamanasaurus primarily consumed low vegetation.
Yamanasaurus lojaensis is the type and only species within its genus.
Taxonomically, it belongs to the family Saltasauridae and the parent group Saltasaurinae.
The animal is classified within the broader class Saurischia.
This dinosaur inhabited Ecuador during the Campanian-Maastrichtian stage of the late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 70 million years ago.
Its existence spanned the Maastrichtian period, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
